On that unit the device answered the opening request, both EQs read back what the bridge pushed (all five filter types, the pre-gain, both ends of every limit), a save to memory 22 could be loaded back, and a headphone-EQ push took on both channels and left the user EQ alone. The firmware stores what its fields hold rather than the editor's limits (gain to ±51.1 dB, Q just under 16), and stores a band written while the EQ is off; what its DSP does with values past the editor's limits was not measured, so the ranges stay the app's. In single-EQ mode the bridge read and wrote every band of the all-band EQ and refused the headphone EQ. The app shows the same firmware version and, for the memory the bridge saved, the same values. An EQ pushed without saving was still there after the device was unplugged and powered off and on. Other operating systems were not checked. Identity: the app lists eleven product ids under vendor 0x0a12 and accepts a device only when its product name contains "Qudelix". A match can't say "contains", so the first entry takes the ids with any name. The two names recorded are kept as more specific entries: 0x4005 "Qudelix-5K USB DAC 48KHz" from devicePEQ's capture and 0x4007 "Qudelix-5K USB DAC" from a maintainer's unit. The other nine names are unknown, and nothing in the app says what tells the ids apart (perhaps the USB audio setting). 0x0a12 is the Bluetooth chip vendor's id, shared with other makers (FiiO's among them), so the vendor alone says nothing. Firmware: the app refuses firmware below 2.0.0 and asks for an update. Firmware 2.x has another EQ layout (one 20-band EQ, or 10 bands per channel) with other filter codes, which the bridge does not drive: only 3.0.0 and later is driven. On 3.x the user EQ has 10 bands on one channel, layered on a headphone EQ of 10 bands per channel; in single-EQ mode ("USR only" in the app) one all-band EQ of 20 bands replaces both, and the bridge drives that one and reports 20 bands. In the QX-over output mode the app warns that the device supports a 10-band EQ only. This profile describes the user EQ. The headphone EQ has its own values: 10 bands per channel (left and right), parametric only, the same limits, a pre-gain per channel, and as presets Flat (0) and 20 memories of its own (22 to 41); in the QX-over output mode the app offers the built-in curves on it too. It does not exist in single-EQ mode. It is listed as the device's other EQ (protocol.eqs) with its left and right channels independent. On 2026-11-21 the same unit was sent one band write on the headphone EQ for the right channel alone (channel mask 2), which changed the right channel and left the left as it was, and one for the left alone (mask 1), which changed the left only; its stored preset then read back the two channels apart. A push through the bridge of a different curve and pre-gain on each channel read back as written, the user EQ untouched. So the bridge writes and reads them apart, as the app's selector does; a push without the right channel writes both alike. The graphic EQ, crossfeed, headroom, the QX-over crossover and the device's other settings are not driven. Before 2026-11-19 this profile was seeded from AutoEQ's optimizer setting: 20 to 20000 Hz, ±12 dB, Q 103/1024 to 7, peaking and shelves only, pre-gain unknown. The app's editor is wider on every range and adds low-pass and high-pass. AutoEQ's Q ceiling of 7 fits the 13-bit Q field of firmware 2.x (just under 8 in 1/1024ths); the 14-bit field of 3.x holds the app's 15. devicePEQ's handler, which the bridge's first version was ported from, wrote both channels of the user EQ where the app writes its one, saved and loaded memories the way firmware 2.x takes them, never sent the opening request the device answers (so it saw no answers and called the device write-only), and devicePEQ dropped the device for that.

The device can report five channels for the user EQ instead of one (front, center, LFE, back, side; likely in its surround USB mode), and the app then edits one at a time. The user EQ keeps 10 memories (22 to 31). This profile describes the user EQ. The headphone EQ has its own values: 10 bands per channel, parametric only, the same limits and a pre-gain per channel, on 2, 4 or 8 channels (left and right; the QX-over's low and high; or a multi-driver earphone's drivers), with Flat (0) and 20, 5 or 5 memories of its own (from 22). It is listed as the device's other EQ (protocol.eqs) with the 20 memories of its 2-channel form, its left and right channels independent: the bridge writes and reads them apart, as the app's selector does, and refuses the EQ on 4 or 8 channels. The app offers the graphic EQ (user EQ only) from firmware 1.5.6; it is not driven, nor are crossfeed, headroom, the per-channel mute and the device's other settings (DAC filter, USB mode, bass boost).

From the User's Guide ADI-2 DAC v1.8, §12.2 Subpage Parametric EQ: band 1 is Peak, Shelf, High Cut or High Pass; bands 2-4 are fixed to Peak; band 5 is Peak, Shelf or High Cut. Gain -12 to +12 dB in 0.5 dB steps. Frequency 20 Hz (200 Hz for bands 4 and 5) to 20 kHz, 'in steps between 1 Hz and 100 Hz': the guide doesn't say where the step changes, so the frequency domains are left continuous and the device rounds. Q 0.5 to 9.9 on bands 1-3 and 0.5 to 5.0 on bands 4-5, in steps of 0.1. Cut and pass filters are 12 dB/oct, at the band's Q. The guide calls the shelf of bands 1 and 5 just 'Shelf' and doesn't say which way it faces: a low shelf on band 1 and a high shelf on band 5 is an assumption to confirm on the device. There is no EQ preamp: the DSP has 24 dB of internal headroom (§13) and Volume must be lowered for large boosts. With Dual EQ on, left and right have their own settings, which v1 profiles don't describe; this profile is the linked (default) setting. Bass/Treble is a separate engine: rme-adi-2-dac-fs-bass-treble. The USB product name carries the unit's serial number ('ADI-2 DAC (51120366)'), so the match uses ids only; they come from a Linux hardware report, not from RME.
